lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: relating domain to a quantitative context
lessonRef.title: Performance task build: relating domain to a quantitative context

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Set up the first two carefully; the rest of the build depends on them.

items.prompt: A machine starts with 110 components and consumes 8 per hour. It can run for at most 13 hours. What is the domain of C(h) = 110 − 8h in this context?
choices: all real numbers

items.prompt: A sequence is defined by a(1) = -2 and a(n) = a(n − 1) + 7 for n > 1. Find a(9).

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: In a modelling context, the graph of a projectile’s height against time crosses the horizontal axis. Which feature is this, and what does it mean?
choices: the maximum, giving the greatest height
the y-intercept, giving the launch height
a zero, giving the time the projectile returns to ground level
the average rate of change over the flight

items.prompt: Does the set {(1, 3), (2, 5), (1, 8), (4, 9)} define y as a function of x? Justify the decision.
choices: Yes; repeated outputs are allowed, only repeated inputs with different outputs are not.
No; the input 4 gives both y = 2 and y = −2.
No; the input 1 is paired with both 3 and 8.
Yes; each input appears once, so each has exactly one output.

items.prompt: A machine starts with 40 components and consumes 4 per hour. It can run for at most 35 hours. What is the domain of C(h) = 40 − 4h in this context?
choices: all real numbers

items.prompt: A sequence is defined by a(1) = -11 and a(n) = a(n − 1) + 9 for n > 1. Find a(20).
In a modelling context, the graph of a cooling object’s temperature flattens out towards a horizontal line. Which feature is this, and what does it mean?
choices: an end behaviour approaching the surrounding temperature
a zero, giving the time the object freezes
a maximum, giving the hottest temperature
an interval of increase

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Carry the build to a result and state the check that would catch an error in it.

items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Does the relation x = y², for real y define y as a function of x? Justify the decision.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
